data.cultural_impact: The name Crispus has Roman origins and was popular during the classical period. In the context of early Christianity, it was adopted as the name of a martyr who, according to tradition, was a treasurer of the Roman emperor Maximianus Herculius and converted to Christianity alongside his wife and son, Bishop Serenus. The story of their conversion is commemorated in the Martyrdom of Saints Crispus, Donatian, and Hippolytus.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Saint Crispus is revered as a martyr who gave up his worldly position and wealth to follow Christ. His story serves as an inspiration for those who are called to renounce their material possessions and embrace a life of faith. The name Crispus could be seen as a symbol of the transformative power of faith, as the Latin root "cris-" also means 'curly', representing the idea of change or transformation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Crispus, derived from the Roman word crispus (curly-haired), was adopted by St. Paul as the name of a Roman centurion who converted to Christianity. This name symbolizes the transformation from a pagan warrior to a follower of Christ, suggesting the spiritual journey from worldly power to divine grace.

biblical_reference.note: Crispus is mentioned as the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth who believed in the Lord with his household

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Crispus was the name of a son of the Roman Emperor Constantine I. The name Crispus carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Crispus continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Crispus from Dublin, Ireland embodies the meaning of Crispus - "Ancient Roman name". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
